The '''2021 Copa Sudamericana first stage''' was played from 16 March to 14 April 2021.<ref name="calendar">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/calendario_2021_02_10_2020.pdf|title=CALENDÁRIO 2021: CONMEBOL Libertadores - CONMEBOL Sudamericana - RECOPA|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref> A total of 32 teams competed in the first stage to decide 16 of the 32 places in the [[2021 Copa Sudamericana group stage|group stage]] of the [[2021 Copa Sudamericana]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/reglamento-sudamericana-manual-de-clubes-2021-es.pdf|title=Manual de Clubes / Reglamento CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2021|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref>

==Draw==
<section begin=Draw />
The draw for the first stage was held on 5 February 2021, 12:00 [[Time in Paraguay|PYST]] ([[UTC−03:00|UTC−3]]), at the CONMEBOL Convention Centre in [[Luque]], [[Paraguay]].<ref name="First stage draw">{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/es/este-viernes-se-sortea-el-camino-para-las-competiciones-de-clubes-2021|title=Este viernes se sortea el camino para las competiciones de clubes 2021|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=2 February 2021|language=es}}</ref><ref name="fixture">{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/es/inicia-el-camino-hacia-la-gran-conquista|title=Inicia el camino hacia La Gran Conquista|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=5 February 2021|language=es}}</ref> For the first stage, the 32 teams involved were divided into eight pots according to their national association.

The 32 teams were drawn into 16 ties, with the four teams from each national association drawn against each other into two ties per association (e.g., the four teams from Bolivia were drawn into ties BOL 1 and BOL 2), and the first team drawn in each tie hosting the second leg.<section end=Draw />

==Format==
<section begin=Format />
In the first stage, each tie was played on a home-and-away [[two-legged tie|two-legged]] basis. If tied on aggregate, the [[away goals rule]] was used. If still tied, [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] will not be played, and a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] would be used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 2.4.2).<ref name="regulations"/>

The 16 winners of the first stage advanced to the [[2021 Copa Sudamericana group stage|group stage]] to join the 12 teams directly qualified for that stage (six from Argentina and six from Brazil), and four teams transferred from the [[2021 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] (the four teams eliminated in the [[2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Third stage|third stage]] of [[2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages|qualifying]]).<section end=Format />

==Matches==
The first legs were played on 16–18 March, 6 and 7 April while the second legs were played on 6–8, 13 and 14 April 2021.<ref name="fixture"/><ref name="fixture_pdf">{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/fixture_conmebol_sudamericana_primera_fase_05_02_2021.pdf|title=CONMEBOL SUDAMERICANA 2021 PROGRAMA DE PARTIDOS - Departamento de Competiciones Versión de 05/02/2021|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=5 February 2021|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/fixture_conmebol_sudamericana_primera_fase_10_03_2021.pdf|title=CONMEBOL SUDAMERICANA 2021 PROGRAMA DE PARTIDOS - Departamento de Competiciones Versión de 10/03/2021|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=10 March 2021|language=es}}</ref>
